VoiceOver Image Descriptions in iOS vs zh-Hans listing copy — two different jobs

Teams assume VoiceOver Image Descriptions working on buyer devices covers storefront language. On-device spoken alt text and Connect actually separate image-description behavior from product-page copy:

  • VoiceOver Image Descriptions in Settings — Settings → Accessibility → VoiceOver → Image Descriptions lets VoiceOver speak descriptions of images in Photos, Safari, Messages, Mail, and supported apps. Labeled 图像描述 or 图片描述 in zh-Hans system UI. Does not generate Chinese App Store listing text.
  • Describe Images in the VoiceOver rotor — buyer-visible action that triggers a spoken description of the focused image. Your listing may show rotor menus or before/after description playback on gallery frames; building caption backends is engineering work, not Connect metadata.
  • In-app alt text and image narration — third-party apps that generate or display spoken descriptions, automatic alt text for uploaded photos, or accessibility image captions for blind users. Listing copy describes the benefit; on-device caption models live in the binary.
  • Pricing and Availability → China — makes the app downloadable on the China App Store. Separate from language rows.
  • App Store tab → Chinese (Simplified) localization — independent row for title, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text, screenshots, and caption lines. Empty or English here means China buyers see English fallback regardless of Image Descriptions support in iOS or your app.

Image Descriptions working on buyer devices and a localized China listing are both required when you sell on the China storefront — neither replaces the other. AppLocale covers how you describe VoiceOver Image Descriptions, Describe Images, and 图像描述 value on the product page in zh-Hans, not how you implement caption models or VoiceOver APIs in code.

Image Descriptions-specific listing vocabulary — what translates differently

Accessibility image-description marketing on App Store pages uses vocabulary general VoiceOver or photo guides rarely cover. zh-Hans copy should reflect how Chinese blind and low-vision buyers describe spoken alt text — not a literal paste of US marketing:

Image Descriptions vs general VoiceOver

US pages use "Works with VoiceOver" or "VoiceOver support" for general screen reader compatibility. Image Descriptions as-lead copy should name the specific feature — Image Descriptions, Describe Images, spoken alt text — using 图像描述, 图片描述, or 描述图像 when your app or marketing aligns with Apple's VoiceOver Image Descriptions setting, not generic 旁白支持 alone.

Image Descriptions vs Visual Look Up

Visual Look Up identifies plants, pets, and landmarks for sighted users — 视觉查找, 识别植物. Image Descriptions speaks what is in a photo for users who cannot see it — 图像描述, 朗读图像内容. Do not paste 识别植物 copy onto Image Descriptions hero frames; see Visual Look Up listing (zh-Hans, contrast).

Image Descriptions vs Live Text and Point and Speak

Live Text extracts editable text — 实况文本. Magnifier Point and Speak reads physical text the camera points at — 检测模式, 指点并朗读. Image Descriptions narrates image scenes for blind users — different Connect string family. See Live Text and Magnifier guides for contrast vocabulary only.

Subtitle and keyword packing

The 30-character subtitle and 100-character keyword field need accessibility-relevant search terms Chinese buyers type — see Simplified Chinese keywords & subtitle for field mechanics. Terms like 图像描述, 图片描述, 旁白, and 视障 each signal different intent from generic photo-app keywords.
